comparisons.peer_summary: Multiple lawsuits alleging LIBOR manipulation by the Corporation, BANA, and other banks remain pending in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, with motions for summary judgment currently pending for remaining claims involving individual and class plaintiffs.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Bank of America are both defendants in antitrust class actions involving alleged manipulation of financial benchmarks (CDS for GS and LIBOR for BAC), with both proceedings located in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. A meaningful difference exists in the litigation status as of December 2024: Goldman Sachs’ proceedings were stayed pending enforcement of a 2015 settlement, while Bank of America’s remaining LIBOR claims were active with motions for summary judgment pending. Both cases assert claims under federal antitrust law and the Commodity Exchange Act, but GS had already navigated a significant portion of the litigation through prior settlements and jurisdictional dismissals, whereas BAC was awaiting summary judgment rulings on remaining individual and class claims.

sentences.text: Group Inc., GS&Co. and GSI were among the defendants named in a putative antitrust class action relating to the settlement of credit default swaps, filed on June 30, 2021 in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Mexico.

The complaint generally asserts claims under federal antitrust law and the Commodity Exchange Act in connection with an alleged conspiracy among the defendants to manipulate the benchmark price used to value credit default swaps for settlement.

On January 24, 2024, the court granted the defendants' motion to stay the proceedings pending the resolution of the motion filed by the defendants on November 3, 2023 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York to enforce a 2015 settlement and release among the parties.
Beginning in 2011, several individual and putative class actions were filed against the Corporation, BANA, and certain Merrill Lynch entities, as well as other banks on the U.S. Dollar LIBOR panel.

These actions alleged that defendants manipulated LIBOR during the financial crisis and asserted a variety of claims, including federal and state antitrust, Commodity Exchange Act, Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act, Securities Exchange Act of 1934, common law fraud, and breach of contract claims and sought compensatory, treble and punitive damages, and injunctive relief.
All remaining cases are pending in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

Defendants' motion for summary judgment is pending on all remaining claims, brought by individual plaintiffs and one class of plaintiffs who purchased over-the-counter instruments incorporating LIBOR.

comparisons.peer_topic: Mexican Government Bonds Antitrust Litigation Status
comparisons.peer_summary: A putative class action alleging collusion in the Mexican sovereign bond market was reinstated by the US Court of Appeals in February 2024, leading to a third amended complaint in June 2024 and the denial of a motion to dismiss in January 2025; claims against Citigroup affiliates were previously dismissed.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Citigroup are defendants in significant antitrust class actions concerning the manipulation of benchmark prices for financial instruments (CDS and Mexican Government Bonds, respectively). A key similarity is the judicial outcome regarding the viability of the claims: GS had its claims against certain foreign defendants dismissed for lack of personal jurisdiction while remaining claims against US entities proceeded (though later stayed), whereas Citigroup initially had its case dismissed in 2019, only to have that dismissal vacated and the case reinstated by the Court of Appeals in February 2024. In both cases, the proceedings involve allegations of conspiracy to manipulate benchmark prices/settlement values, but the procedural status diverged with GS moving to a stay and C moving to a third amended complaint and renewed motion to dismiss.

The complaint generally asserts claims under federal antitrust law and the Commodity Exchange Act in connection with an alleged conspiracy among the defendants to manipulate the benchmark price used to value credit default swaps for settlement.

On June 5, 2023, the court dismissed the claims against certain foreign defendants for lack of personal jurisdiction but denied the defendants' motion to dismiss with respect to GS&Co., GSI and the remaining defendants.

Antitrust and Other Litigation: In 2018, a putative class action was filed against Citigroup, CGMI, Citigroup Financial Products Inc., Citigroup Global Markets Holdings Inc., Banamex, Grupo Banamex, and other banks, captioned IN RE MEXICAN GOVERNMENT BONDS ANTITRUST LITIGATION, in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York.
The complaint alleges that defendants colluded in the Mexican sovereign bond market.
In September 2019, the court granted defendants' motion to dismiss.
On July 29, 2024, certain defendants, including Banamex, filed a motion to dismiss the third amended complaint.

Both cases were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. However, their procedural outcomes in 2024 differed significantly: Morgan Stanley reached an agreement in principle to settle class claims in February 2024 following a denial of class certification, whereas Goldman Sachs saw its proceedings stayed in January 2024 pending a motion to enforce a prior 2015 settlement. sentences.text: Group Inc., GS&Co. and GSI were among the defendants named in a putative antitrust class action relating to the settlement of credit default swaps, filed on June 30, 2021 in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Mexico.

The complaint generally asserts claims under federal antitrust law and the Commodity Exchange Act in connection with an alleged conspiracy among the defendants to manipulate the benchmark price used to value credit default swaps for settlement.

On January 24, 2024, the court granted the defendants' motion to stay the proceedings pending the resolution of the motion filed by the defendants on November 3, 2023 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York to enforce a 2015 settlement and release among the parties.

Beginning in February of 2016, the Firm was named as a defendant in multiple purported antitrust class actions now consolidated into a single proceeding in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York ("SDNY") styled In Re: Interest Rate Swaps Antitrust Litigation.

Plaintiffs allege, inter alia, that the Firm, together with a number of other financial institution defendants, violated U.S. and New York state antitrust laws from 2008 through December of 2016 in connection with alleged efforts to prevent the development of electronic exchange-based platforms for interest rate swaps trading.
On December 15, 2023, the court denied the class plaintiffs' motion for class certification.
